catalog_quote: Moreover, Mätro nDrapa has word tones in which a phonological word’s first two syllables have one of the following pitch patterns, while the third and further syllables are unstressed and have low pitch value (low-level pitch is left unmarked in phonemic transcription): (i) high-level (σ́/σ́σ́), (ii) high-falling (σ̂/σ́σ [σ́σ̀]), (iii) low-rising (σ̌/σσ́ [σ̀σ́]), and (iv) low-rising-falling (σ̌σ [σ̌σ̀]). Tones may vary, however, in accordance with post-lexical prosody that reflects certain contexts, including the information structure (Shirai 2019). Most affixes and clitics (including classifiers with a few exceptions) do not have a specific tone but do become part of the host’s phonological word. ... [n.6] In the Mätro dialect, the low-rising-falling tone is not attested in monosyllabic words.

new_statements.rule_in_words: nDrapa is a word-tone language: the tone-bearing unit is the phonological word (root plus toneless affixes/clitics), and one of four tonal melodies is realised over its first two syllables; syllables from the third onward are unstressed, low-pitched (and, per Shirai 2019: 36 and Suzuki 2006: 110, low/mid and shortened). Prominence is thus confined to the word-initial two-syllable window; no single stressed syllable or positional stress rule beyond this is given.
new_statements.secondary_stress: None described; third and later syllables of the phonological word are explicitly unstressed/low.
new_statements.exceptions: Tones vary with post-lexical prosody/information structure (Shirai 2019); a few classifiers and emphasised enclitics (e.g. causative =ʈhu, sentence-final particles) can form their own phonological word bearing their own tone and stress (Shirai 2007 n.9; Shirai 2019 causative chapter ex. 7); low-rising-falling tone not attested on monosyllables (n.6). Other analysts (Huang Bufan 1991/2009, Gong 2007, Liu et al. 2005) treat other dialects as syllable-tone languages.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the phonological word (host + toneless affixes and clitics, may span several grammatical words); statement is for the Mätro (Northern) dialect in citation/lexical forms, with post-lexical variation acknowledged. Corroborated instrumentally for Nyato (Southern) by Shirai 2019 and impressionistically for Ngwirdei (Northern) by Suzuki 2006.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement describes the Mätro (Mazhong 麻中 village, Zhongni township, Daofu) dialect of the Northern nDrapa dialect group; Shirai 2019 (Nyato, Southern group, Yajiang) and Suzuki 2006 (Ngwirdei/Hongding, Northern) report the same word-tone architecture (first two syllables distinctive, third and later low). Gong 2007 (Woduo/瓦多, Southern) and Huang Bufan 1990/1991/2009 (Zhatuo, Northern) analyse syllable tone instead. CAUTION: the phonology in the English/Chinese Wikipedia 'Zhaba language' articles comes from Namkung 1996, whose 'Zhaba' entry (Sun et al. 1991 ZMYYC #16, Tuanjie, Yajiang) is Queyu (quey1238), not nDrapa — Namkung p.453 n.1 says so explicitly; the earlier scan's '4 tones via Namkung' therefore does not belong to zhab1238.
